objectives.statement: Represent fractions, including fractions equal to or greater than 1, on area models and a number line, naming the whole each fraction refers to.
Add and subtract fractions with like denominators, and with related denominators (e.g. halves, quarters, eighths), by using equivalent fractions.
Compare and order fractions using benchmarks (0, 1/2, 1), common denominators and the number line, and justify each comparison.

content.body: Use one bar as one kilogram. Equal parts must have the same size. Five fourths fills one whole bar and one quarter of another equal bar. On a number line, each interval of length one is one whole. Locate 5/4 between 1 and 2.

prompts.prompt: Sketch 1 and 3/2 on equal bars and on a number line. Name the whole and explain why 3/2 exceeds 1.

Count five quarter-steps from zero; one unit is one kilogram. A number line from 0 to 2 marked in 4ths. 2/3 is the same amount as 4/6, 8/12. The same whole and amount: 2/3 = 4/6 = 8/12. Sketch 1 and 3/2 on equal bars and on a number line. Name the whole and explain why 3/2 exceeds 1.

content.body: An exact fraction is the primary answer. Equivalent fractions such as 5/6 and 10/12 are equally correct. A finite decimal is equivalent only when exactly equal, such as 3/4 = 0.75. Here 5/6 is not equal to 0.83. Only a question explicitly requesting rounding accepts 0.83 as an approximation to two decimal places.

content.body: Synthetic seed-bank task. A group has 3/4 kg and packs 1/3 kg. Write the exact remainder as a fraction and justify its size. Then, as a separate estimate, round the remainder to two decimal places, using the third decimal digit and rounding a halfway value up. Write approximately equal for the estimate.

prompts.prompt: Give the exact remaining mass and the approximation to two decimal places. Explain why the remainder is positive and smaller than 3/4 kg.
